title: Social media addiction affects older adults too
content_md: Social media addiction is often discussed as a problem affecting teenagers. Yet older adults can also spend more time on social platforms than they intend , lose track of their day and find it difficult to put their phones down. This article looks at why social media can become so absorbing, how to spot unhealthy habits and how older users can stay connected without letting scrolling take over. I will also explain why social media is not inherently harmful because it offers older people a practical way to maintain relationships, find communities and stay involved with the wider world. The aim is not to encourage you to abandon social media. It is to help you use these platforms more safely . Key takeaways Social media addiction can affect people of any age. Infinite feeds and personalized recommendations can encourage automatic scrolling. Social media can help older adults maintain relationships and find new communities. Purposeful use is generally more meaningful than endless passive consumption. Privacy checks and scam awareness should form part of a healthier digital routine.
